Synopsis

Three malicious node-ipc npm releases were published on May 14, 2026, adding an obfuscated runtime payload that attempted to collect developer, cloud, SSH, and CI/CD secrets.

Story

This was a new node-ipc supply-chain event, separate from the 2022 protestware incident. On 2026-05-14, the npm package received three new releases across active and legacy version lines: 12.0.1, 9.2.3, and 9.1.6.

StepSecurity reported the releases as malicious and said the payload fired when the package was required at runtime, then attempted to exfiltrate cloud credentials, SSH keys, and CI/CD secrets to external command-and-control infrastructure. Socket independently described the same event as a developing npm compromise with obfuscated stealer and backdoor behavior.

Registry metadata showed the releases were published minutes apart by the `atiertant` npm account. Static comparison against 12.0.0 showed the main ESM file unchanged, while `node-ipc.cjs` gained a large obfuscated block appended after the legitimate exports. That made CommonJS consumers the visible execution path in the sampled tarballs.

The package still looked like node-ipc: the normal package name, repository metadata, README, certificates, and API files were present. The trust break was in the official distribution channel, where a fresh install or permissive semver range could resolve to the malicious release without a downstream code review.
